    AI Overview
    A rollover crash is a dangerous type of accident where a vehicle tips onto its side or roof, often resulting from high speeds, sharp turns, or "tripping" over obstacles like curbs or soft soil. These crashes are frequently fatal, accounting for nearly one-third of all traffic deaths, and are most common in SUVs, pickups, and trucks. 
    Key Aspects of Rollover Crashes 
    • Definition: The vehicle rotates 90 degrees or more, landing on its side or top, often rolling over multiple times.
    • Types of Rollovers:
      • Tripped (95% of single-vehicle rollovers): Occurs when a vehicle leaves the roadway and strikes an object (curb, guardrail, ditch) or soft soil, causing it to flip.
      • Untripped: Caused by reckless steering or high-speed maneuvers that force the vehicle to lose grip and flip, common in taller vehicles with higher centers of gravity.
    • Common Causes: Speeding is the primary factor, with over 70% of fatal rollovers occurring in speed zones of 55 mph or higher. Other factors include drunk driving, sudden overcorrection, and poor road conditions.
    • Danger Factors: These crashes are violent, often causing structural damage to the roof ("cabin intrusion") and increasing the risk of occupant ejection.
    • Vehicle Types: SUVs, pickups, and vans are more prone to rollovers due to their higher center of gravity. 
    Rollover accidents are more common on rural roads and often involve only one vehicle.

    Can you survive a rollover crash?
    An error has occurred. Please try again later.
    How does a rollover crash happen?
    It occurs when a car's tire hits something — such as a curb or ditch — that shifts the vehicle's weight to one side, causing it to roll before it can regain its balance. Speeding: If you speed around a curve or take a turn too fast, the tires can lose their grip on the road, leading to a vehicle rollover.

    What happens to your body in a rollover accident?
    As your car rolls, you will be tossed around the car, making contact with various objects before coming to a rest. Your body is at the mercy of elements outside of your control. During a rollover accident, you will go wherever the car goes. It is especially dangerous if you neglect to wear a seat belt.
